clue.text: Flapper has to call a doctor back

parts.note: to buzz someone is to give them a phone call

indicators.note: back tells us the doctor's abbreviation is written in the reverse direction

explanation.surface: Someone (a flapper girl of the 1920s, perhaps) needs to ring for a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flapper' suggests a 1920s party girl, but here it is anything that flaps its wings. 'back' turns DR into RD.
explanation.definitionFit: A buzzard is a large bird of prey, and birds are creatures whose wings flap, so a playful description fits.

clue.text: Lie next to Clio for one puzzle

parts.note: to lie is to be somewhere or simply exist, as in let it lie, let it be
Clio is the Muse of history, one of the nine Muses

explanation.surface: Someone lies down beside Clio, a figure who is a riddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemuse someone is to confuse or bewilder them, which is what puzzling them means.

clue.text: Zulu minister needs to acquire spectacles to get a closer look

indicators.note: to acquire is to take in, so the spectacles go inside the other letters

parts.note: Zulu is the NATO alphabet word for Z
OO looks like a pair of round glasses

explanation.surface: A Zulu clergyman needs glasses to see more clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: To zoom in is to magnify the view with a lens, so the viewer gets a closer look.

clue.text: Dutch settler sees naked friar running

indicators.note: running about suggests disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Dutch settler spots a monk streaking past without clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Afrikander is an older term for an Afrikaner, a South African descended from Dutch colonists.

clue.text: Brick carrier reflected: "Hey, the Japanese can compete here"

indicators.note: a reflection shows things backwards, so the carrier's name is reversed

parts.note: a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks
yo is a slang greeting like hey

explanation.surface: A builder shouts a greeting at his reflection, mentioning a Japanese contest venue.
explanation.definitionFit: The dohyo is the raised clay ring where sumo wrestlers fight, a Japanese contest arena.

clue.text: Man exposing pecker on stage

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another follows it, so the bird comes after the stage

parts.note: a step is a stage in a process
a hen pecks at its food, so it is a pecker

explanation.surface: A man is caught showing off something rude in front of a theatre audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pecker' has a vulgar slang sense the surface leans on; here it is simply a bird that pecks.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen is a boy's given name, so any man so called is one example of a man.

clue.text: Woman tempted by house with small bedroom makes note

parts.note: a semi is a British semi-detached house
BR is the abbreviation for bedroom in property listings
Eve was the woman tempted by the serpent in Eden

explanation.surface: A woman is lured by a house with a little bedroom and writes a memo.
explanation.walkthrough: A SEMI is a British semi-detached house, sharing one wall with its neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A semibreve is the musical note lasting four beats, the whole note.

clue.text: 10 stone flying bird

indicators.note: flying here means flying off, so the weight's letters leave the name

parts.note: 10 across is the author Hemingway, whose first name is Ernest
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

explanation.surface: Ten stone of bird in flight, a heavy flier.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' points to 10 across, HEMINGWAY, whose first name ERNEST loses ST when 'flying'.
explanation.definitionFit: An erne is a sea eagle, a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Who incorrectly said it's a gun?

indicators.note: incorrectly means wrongly arranged, so the letters of Who are shuffled
said tells us we write how the phrase is pronounced

parts.note: spoken quickly, it's a has the same sound as the end of the answer

explanation.surface: Someone asking who misreported that something is a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: A howitzer is a short artillery piece that fires shells on a high trajectory, a kind of gun.

clue.text: I oppose, in fact, state hospital drama

parts.note: nay is used to introduce a stronger statement, much like in fact
to say is to state
ER was a long-running US hospital TV drama

explanation.surface: A protester declares opposition, really, to a TV medical drama about the state.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is what the answer says: a person who always says 'I oppose'.
explanation.definitionFit: A naysayer habitually objects or denies, so their constant refrain is a declaration of opposition.

clue.text: Beast from horror shows

indicators.note: the clue's words show the answer by displaying it inside themselves, spread across two words

explanation.surface: A monster has come out of a horror film or show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' signals the letters are on display in 'from horror', straddling the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The mhorr is a North African gazelle, an animal, and a beast is any animal.

clue.text: Women extremely happy to get involved with Enigma author

indicators.note: letters that get involved with one another are mixed up together, so this pool is rearranged
extremely asks for only the extreme letters of happy, its first and last

explanation.surface: Women are very keen to be part of some Enigma project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get involved' shuffles W, HY (the outer letters of 'happy') and ENIGMA into the author's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Hemingway was an American novelist, writer of The Old Man and the Sea, so he is an author.

clue.text: After unpleasant brouhaha, fails to find causes of stench

indicators.note: After places the word for fails behind the word for the fuss in the answer

parts.note: to kick up a stink is to make an unpleasant fuss or brouhaha
a show that bombs is a flop, so bombs means fails

explanation.surface: After an ugly row, someone fails to track down where a bad smell comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Stink bombs are small capsules made to release a foul smell, so they are causes of a stench.

clue.text: Ancient books devoured by a son in retreat where philosophers gathered

indicators.note: a retreating army goes backwards, so the whole assembly is read in reverse
something devoured by another ends up inside it, so the books go into the pair of letters

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
OT is the Old Testament, the Bible's older books

explanation.surface: Old volumes are eaten up by a boy hiding away somewhere philosophers once met.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devoured by' puts OT inside AS, giving AOTS; 'in retreat' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stoa was a covered colonnade in Athens where Zeno taught, giving the Stoic philosophers their name.

clue.text: Inflammation that's dire when daughter goes — it hurts badly

indicators.note: badly means in a wrong way, so the letters are put into disorder
the daughter goes, leaving the word dire, so her letter is removed from it

parts.note: D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A dreadful swelling causes great pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when daughter goes' takes D from DIRE, leaving IRE, and 'badly' shuffles that with IT HURTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Urethritis is a painful swelling of the urethra, a kind of inflammation.

clue.text: Eye raves possibly in this time for partying

parts.note: this points at the answer: read as an instruction, its first word asks for a fresh arrangement of the rest, and that arrangement could be Eye raves

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark that eyes go wild on a particular party night.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'Eye raves' is the result of following the answer as wordplay, with NEW as the anagram signal acting on YEARS EVE. 'possibly' admits the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The night of 31 December is the traditional occasion for parties seeing in the coming twelve months.

clue.text: Used to be cool to carry loaded gun in cleansing operation

parts.note: was is the past tense of be

indicators.note: to carry is to hold within, so the shuffled weapon sits inside the word for cool

parts.note: hip means fashionable, cool

indicators.note: loaded suggests drunk and unsteady, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone who was trendy carries a loaded weapon during a clean-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded' is the anagram signal on 'gun', not a description of it; 'to carry' then holds the result within the word for cool.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing-up is British for doing the dishes after a meal, a cleaning job.

clue.text: Plans to hold religious classes in French cathedral

indicators.note: to hold is to contain, so the classes go inside the word for plans

parts.note: charts are plans or maps
RE is religious education in British schools

explanation.surface: Plans are made for religious lessons in a French cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is religious education in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartres, south-west of Paris, is famous for its Gothic cathedral, so the town names the cathedral.

clue.text: Angry viewer has strabismus

parts.note: cross means angry
an eye is what sees, a viewer

explanation.surface: A furious spectator turns out to have a squint.
explanation.definitionFit: Strabismus is the medical name for a squint, where the eyes look in different directions.

clue.text: Husband's rottenness stirred up hostile reaction

indicators.note: stirred up means mixed around, so the letters of rottenness are rearranged

explanation.surface: A husband's foul behaviour provoked an angry response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirred up' rearranges ROTTENNESS to follow H.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up a hornets' nest is the idiom for provoking angry opposition, so the phrase names that hostility.

clue.text: Felt ruthless somewhat picking up swimmer

indicators.note: in a down answer, picking up means lifting, so the run of letters is read upwards
somewhat means only part of these words is used

explanation.surface: Someone felt pitiless when lifting a swimmer from the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' takes ELTRUT from 'Felt ruthless'; 'picking up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A turtle is a reptile that lives in water and moves with flippers, so it is a swimmer.

clue.text: Nymph on a cycle shows liveliness

indicators.note: a cycle sends the last letter round to the front

parts.note: a sprite is a fairy or nymph

explanation.surface: A fairy riding a bicycle displays great vivacity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a cycle' moves the last E of SPRITE to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit, from French, means spirit and wit, a sparkle or liveliness.

clue.text: She was revolting

definitions.meaning: ... is a woman's name, so she could be ...
... is the past tense of rise, as in people who ... up in revolt

explanation.surface: A woman who behaved disgustingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' reads as disgusting, but here it means rebelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising is an uprising, so those who rose were rebelling; Rose is also a common female forename.

clue.text: Biscuits made by nuns, largely trigger happy

indicators.note: trigger happy suggests wild, reckless behaviour, signalling the letters are scrambled
largely means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Biscuits baked by nuns who are mostly quick on the trigger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' cuts 'trigger' to TRIGGE; 'happy' mixes that with NUNS. 'trigger happy' looks like one phrase but is split between the two jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger nuts are hard ginger-flavoured British biscuits, a teatime staple.

clue.text: Type of wildebeest seen across Spain

indicators.note: the animals are spread across the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: gnus are wildebeest; the plural form
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A kind of wildebeest spotted crossing Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus is a class or kind in biology, ranking above species, so it is a type.

clue.text: Sailor's love for a DJ

indicators.note: for means in place of, so the zero replaces the letter a

parts.note: Jack, as in Jack Tar, is a sailor
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A seaman's affection for a disc jockey.
explanation.definitionFit: Jock is a slangy short form of disc jockey, the person who plays records.

clue.text: Daughter in play annoyed about parts for harmonium?

indicators.note: the daughter's name parts, opening up to make room for the other piece

parts.note: Regan is one of King Lear's daughters in Shakespeare's play

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for annoyed is reversed

parts.note: to rode someone is an old sense of harassing or annoying them, as in rode roughshod

explanation.surface: A girl acting in a play gets annoyed over the parts written for a harmonium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the word for annoyed and 'parts for' opens the daughter's name around it. Rode is from ride, to harass; the question mark marks the harmonium as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonium is a small keyboard instrument whose sound comes from air pumped over free reeds.

clue.text: I appreciate that time's needed with Arabic language

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone says thanks while noting time and Arabic are both needed for a language.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatar is a Turkic tongue spoken in Tatarstan in Russia, so it is a language.

clue.text: Take a nip across summit? Come again?

indicators.note: the word for drinking stretches across the other word, holding it inside

parts.note: to sup is to sip a drink, taking a nip
a peak is a mountain summit

explanation.surface: A climber takes a quick drink on the mountaintop and asks someone to repeat themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Come again? asks someone to repeat what they said louder, which is the request made by saying speak up.

clue.text: Dubious American priest admitted to cult

indicators.note: someone admitted to a group gets inside it, so these pieces go within the word for cult

parts.note: a sect is a religious cult
US is short for United States, hence American

explanation.surface: A shady American cleric has been let into a cult.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suspect is open to doubt or questionable, which is what dubious means.
